title: Dutch Defense: the ideas
line: From the first move, Black fights for the center with a pawn from the king's side.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Push the pawn on f7 two squares. It fights for e4, a center square.

also.g8f6: That leads to the Indian defenses, also sound. This lesson goes on with the pawn on f7.
also.d7d5: That leads to the Queen's Gambit, also sound. This lesson goes on with the pawn on f7.

steps.after: This is the Dutch Defense. The pawn move loosens the squares near Black's king, a risk Black takes on.

steps.text: Bring the knight out. With the pawn, it holds e4.
Move the pawn in front of your king one square, to free your bishop.

also.g7g6: That is the Leningrad Variation, also sound. This lesson goes on with the other pawn.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out, so that your king can castle.
Castle, to get your king to safety.
Move the pawn in front of your queen one square. It keeps White's pieces out of e5.
Step the queen out to e8. From there it can swing across to the king's side.

steps.after: The queen joins the knight on the king's side, and the pawn on f5 still holds e4.

summary: A pawn from the king's side fights for the center at once, and Black's pieces gather to attack the king.
